about: the check of a file with variants, none chosen (the launcher says to choose one)

findings.message: the file defines variants, and a check or a run is of one of them: give --variant <name> with one of small, quiet (none of them is the default)

err: error: the file defines variants, and a check or a run is of one of them: give --variant <name> with one of small, quiet (none of them is the default)
usage: vehicle_sil_launch check [--json] [--strict] [--variant <name>] [--scenario <file> [--param <name>=<value>]...]
[--describe-timeout-ms <ms>] [--connect <network>=<target>]...
[--time-policy realtime|free]
[--disable <name>]... [--enable <name>]... [--manual <name>]... [--] <file>
vehicle_sil_launch run [--json | --events [--events-stall-ms <ms>]] [--stdin-commands] [--start-paused]
[--control <address> [--control-credentials <file>] [--control-tls-cert <file>
--control-tls-key <file>] [--control-audit-log <file>]]
[--variant <name>] [--scenario <file> [--param <name>=<value>]... [--timeline <file>]]
[--speed <speed>] [--strict] [--log-dir <dir>]
[--timeout-ms <ms>]
[--describe-timeout-ms <ms>] [--connect <network>=<target>]...
[--time-policy realtime|free]
[--disable <name>]... [--enable <name>]... [--manual <name>]... [--] <file>
vehicle_sil_launch test [--json] [--strict] [--fail-fast] [--variant <name>]... [--param <name>=<value>]...
[--timeout-ms <ms>] [--describe-timeout-ms <ms>] [--time-policy realtime|free]
[--disable <name>]... [--enable <name>]... <file> --scenarios <directory or files>...
vehicle_sil_launch connections [--json] [--network <name>] [--] <file>
vehicle_sil_launch version [--json]
check <file>                compare the simulation configuration <file> (YAML or JSON) with what each
ecu_main executable in it reports (--describe); list the participants,
the networks and every error and warning
run <file>                  check <file>; if it passes, run the simulation: the registry and the
controller in this process, each participant as a process of its own
(its output on stderr, each line after [<name>]); then end every
participant and report how each ended. Ctrl+C stops it in order
test <file>                 run every scenario of --scenarios with <file>, once for each of its variants, one
run after the other (each as run --speed max --scenario: its own registry and
processes); then a table of all runs: passed, FAILED or skipped, and why. A
failed run does not end the test. Ctrl+C stops the current run in order and
leaves the rest out
connections <file>          where each network of <file> can be connected on this computer: asks the bridge
of each can and ethernet network for its list and writes the targets as
--connect lines to copy (connects to nothing)
version                     the version of vehicle_sil_launch (--json: also its formats and features)
--json                      write the result as JSON
--events                    run: write what happens as events on stdout, one JSON object per line, the
result last (nothing on stderr but the launcher's own failures)
--events-stall-ms <ms>      run --events: give up a reader of the events that takes nothing for <ms>, and wait
at most <ms> for it to take the result (1000 or more; default 30000)
--stdin-commands            run: read commands from stdin, one JSON object per line: {"command":"stop"}
stops in order (twice: without waiting); the end of stdin stops as well;
pause, resume, step (with "ms"), run_until (with "at_ms") and speed (with
"value") control the time
--start-paused              run --stdin-commands or --control: stand still at 0 until a resume or step
command (with --control: before the first step, so that a client's writes
take effect at 0)
--control <address>         run: serve the Control API (gRPC) for clients: the ECUs' variables and the
time; <port> (on 127.0.0.1; 0: any free port), <host>:<port> or unix:<path>;
the event control_server and a line say where (only in a build with
VEHICLE_SIL_BUILD_CONTROL_SERVER=ON)
--control-credentials <file> run --control: tokens and roles, one per line: <role> <name> <token>
(every call then needs a token; never put a token on the command line)
--control-tls-cert <file>   run --control: PEM certificate chain of the server (with --control-tls-key: TLS)
--control-tls-key <file>    run --control: PEM private key of the server
--control-audit-log <file>  run --control: append who changed what
--scenario <file>           check: also check the scenario <file> against the participants' variables;
run: then run it: write the ECUs' variables and compare their values at
virtual times, stop the simulation when the scenario is over, and fail if a
step failed (docs/scenario.md; not with --start-paused; with --control the
clients read and stop, and cannot write or move the time)
--variant <name>            the variant of <file> to check or run (its variants: the common part with the
variant's commands, variable maps, params and enabled laid over it); a file
that defines variants needs it: none is the default. test: only this variant
(repeatable); without it, every variant
--param <name>=<value>      with --scenario: the value of the scenario's parameter ${<name>}, over the
scenario's, the file's and the variant's params; repeatable. test: for each
scenario that has the parameter (at least one must)
--scenarios <dir or files>  test: the scenarios: a directory (the files directly in it that end in .yaml,
.yml or .json, in the order of their names) or files, in the order given;
several after one --scenarios (so <file> comes first, or after --); repeatable
--timeline <file>           run --scenario: write what the scenario wrote and saw over the virtual time
(its steps, the written and the sampled values) to <file> as JSON
(docs/simulation-run.md; schema/timeline.schema.json)
--fail-fast                 test: do not run what comes after the first run that fails
--speed <speed>             run: simulation seconds per wall-clock second (1 real time, 2 twice as fast)
or max (as fast as possible); replaces speed in <file>
--strict                    fail on warnings too
--log-dir <dir>             run: also write each participant's output to <dir>/<name>.log
--timeout-ms <ms>           run: abort the simulation if it has not ended <ms> after its start (wall clock;
with --start-paused and --control, from when it stands still before the start);
test: each run
--describe-timeout-ms <ms>  how long one executable may take for --describe (default 10000)
--connect <network>=<target> connect the network <network> of <file> to a real bus at <target>: an
Ethernet adapter, or virtual:<n> or physical:<n> for a CAN channel (connections
<file> lists those of this computer); none: SIL Kit only. check finds the
network's bridge (next to vehicle_sil_launch or on PATH) and asks it --describe;
run starts it before the other participants (as bridge.<network>) and fails if
it ends. Repeatable, each network once
--time-policy realtime|free the time of a run that is connected outside the simulation (by --connect, or by
an enabled participant with role: bridge). realtime (the default): it goes at
speed 1 whatever speed <file> has; another --speed and --start-paused are the
error outside-real-time, and the commands that pause or step it or change its
speed are refused while it runs. free: the speed and the time are yours to
change as in any run; the bridge still carries frames both ways, so what is
connected there sees the simulation pause or run ahead. No effect on other
runs
--network <name>            connections: only the network <name>
--disable <name>            leave the participant <name> out (as enabled: false in <file>); repeatable
--enable <name>             take the participant <name> in (as enabled: true in <file>); repeatable
--manual <name>             you start the participant <name> yourself (from a debugger, say): run does not
start it, prints the command to start it with and waits for it to join, with
no time limit (as manual: true in <file>); repeatable
--help, -h                  this text
--version                   as version
--                          what follows is the file, also if it starts with '-'
exit codes: 0 passed (run: also stopped by a command), 1 errors (with --strict: or warnings; run: also a failed
simulation; test: a run failed or was left out; connections: a list could not be made), 3 the file
cannot be read (run: or the registry cannot be set up), 4 usage, 5 run: a scenario was stopped by a
command before its end, 130 run or test was interrupted (a signal, or its input or output closed)
the file format: docs/simulation-config.md; check: docs/simulation-check.md; run: docs/simulation-run.md;
events and commands: docs/simulation-events.md; scenarios: docs/scenario.md
